proof.surface: GET /auth/whoami on the head binary; go test ./internal/dispatch/routes/ -run Whoami; Dispatch's browser harness (shell.e2e.ts and live.e2e.ts, Chromium)
proof.command: python3 h.py whoami; go test ./internal/dispatch/routes/ -run Whoami -v; bun run e2e -- bunx playwright test e2e/shell.e2e.ts e2e/live.e2e.ts --project=chromium --workers=1
proof.observed: On the binary, with nothing open, whoami answered 200 event_head 6 in 12 ms. I cleared event_horizon and held an insert (id 7) open across a restart. whoami then answered 503 {"code":"EVENT_HEAD_UNAVAILABLE","error":"no event id is proven final yet; ask again"}, and 200 event_head 7 once the insert committed. All 11 whoami route tests pass, TestWhoamiRefusesWhenItCannotReadTheEventHead (EVENT_HEAD_READ_FAILED) among them. Browser suites: 33 passed, 1 skipped. Those include round 13's EVENT_HEAD_UNAVAILABLE test (the page keeps asking) and the EVENT_HEAD_READ_FAILED test (the page stops on 'Couldn't reach Dispatch.' with Retry). As in round 15, EVENT_HEAD_READ_FAILED is shown by the route test and the browser test, not on a live server.
proof.negativeControl: I changed router.go to answer EVENT_HEAD_UNAVAILABLE for every head error, then restored it (jj status clean). With that change, TestWhoamiRefusesWhenItCannotReadTheEventHead fails ('503 EVENT_HEAD_UNAVAILABLE, want 503 EVENT_HEAD_READ_FAILED'), and so does the anonymous-whoami test.
